chapters.chapter: Interface, Node Graph and workspaces (Nuke Studio environments)

capabilities.capability: Node-based compositing: every image operation is a node, and the wired-up graph is the complete, re-renderable recipe for a shot.
capabilities.pro_use: Artists read a shot as a flow from plates to output and can bypass, swap or branch any step without destroying earlier work.

match.note: Doodleberry's recipe is film data (shots.json) run through fixed passes (player, post, captions, mix); there is no user-editable image-processing graph. WP-36 adds a per-shot node compositor.

capabilities.capability: Graph editing with live inspection: connect a viewer to any node to see that step's output.
capabilities.pro_use: Leads debug a comp by stepping through the tree and seeing what each node contributes.

match.note: graph.get and the Studio /graph page show facts, script, voice, shots, picture, mix, final and QA with each node's state and what changed (WP-20); WP-36 makes it the compositor's editor.

capabilities.capability: Properties panel for every node's parameters, with keyframing and a Curve Editor and Dope Sheet for animation timing.
capabilities.pro_use: Compositors animate any control (a grade, a transform) and refine its easing and timing on curves.

match.note: The Studio timeline shows and edits clip layers, emotion and gaze keys; a curve (graph) editor and a camera-keys lane are WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Viewer with channel isolation, A/B wipe comparison, region of interest, zoom and frame scrubbing.
capabilities.pro_use: Checking an alpha, comparing a version against the last one, or focusing on one area of a heavy frame.

match.note: film.preview gives a scrubbable live player; shot.render with a renderer override writes side-by-side files, and film.diff compares two versions frame by frame (WP-19). Channel views are WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Customisable, saveable workspaces and preferences (panel layouts per task).
capabilities.pro_use: Separate layouts for roto, tracking or review, shared as studio defaults.

match.note: Doodleberry is agent-first: commands are the interface (CLI, HTTP, Studio, MCP) and Studio pages are fixed; window layout presets have no counterpart worth building.

capabilities.capability: Compositing and editorial environments in one application, sharing one project (Nuke Studio).
capabilities.pro_use: An editor and a comp artist move between the cut and a shot's comp without exporting.

match.note: The Studio timeline edits shots.json directly and film.cuts assembles cuts from edit.json; dragging shots and lines in the timeline is WP-19.

capabilities.capability: Project settings that fix the frame range, frame rate and full-size output format for the whole script.
capabilities.pro_use: The delivery spec is locked at the start so every node and render agrees on size and timing.

match.note: Size and fps are film fields; the QA bar (qa.run) then measures 1080x1920 at 30 fps on the output.

capabilities.capability: Scripts saved as plain-text files that can be versioned (v001, v002) and read or written by pipeline tools.
capabilities.pro_use: Artists version up for each review; pipelines generate or patch scripts as text.

match.note: Film data is JSON text in git, validated on film.write; versions are git commits and per-film branches (prod.launch).

capabilities.capability: Proxy mode: work and render at a reduced format or scale, then switch back to full resolution with shapes and tracks still in place.
capabilities.pro_use: Fast interaction on heavy plates; the final render is done at full resolution.

match.note: Vector frames are resolution independent and the player preview is scaled live; there is no low-resolution draft render switch. Render-speed work (render only unique stepped frames, static-layer cache) is WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Separate pre-made low-resolution proxy files per Read, chosen automatically.
capabilities.pro_use: Offline/online workflows on large footage.

match.note: No heavy plate footage: sets and characters are drawn from data at render time.

capabilities.capability: A project directory and relative paths so scripts move between machines and the farm.
capabilities.pro_use: Shots are handed to other artists or render nodes without broken file paths.

match.note: Every film is a self-contained folder with repo-relative references; production sessions work in git worktrees.

capabilities.capability: Enlarging a script: render the same comp at a larger output format.
capabilities.pro_use: Up-res deliverables (HD to UHD) without rebuilding the comp.

match.note: Vector rendering makes any size possible by changing shots.json size, and film.render re-stages aspects; a 4K master as a delivery profile is WP-37.

chapters.chapter: Reading and writing images; working with file metadata

capabilities.capability: Read image sequences and movies in many formats (EXR, DPX, TIFF, PNG, JPEG, QuickTime, MXF, NotchLC) with a colourspace per file.
capabilities.pro_use: Bringing plates, CG renders and stock elements into a comp.

match.note: Images enter as puppets (layered drawings, scans, photos, Blender rigs) or set background plates; a generic footage layer in a shot is WP-36 and EXR/OpenImageIO reading is WP-37.

capabilities.capability: Write renders as image sequences or movies with codec, bit depth, compression, alpha and colourspace options.
capabilities.pro_use: EXR to grading, ProRes to editorial, H.264 for review.

match.note: Output is H.264 MP4 by platform profile (and Lottie, Synfig, web player exports); ProRes 4444 and WebM with alpha (shot.alpha), GIF and APNG (film.formats); EXR masters are WP-37.

capabilities.capability: Multi-layer EXR input and output carrying many named passes in one file.
capabilities.pro_use: CG lighters deliver one EXR per frame with all AOVs; comps write multi-pass masters.

match.note: film.master writes multi-layer EXRs (beauty, line, fill, matte) per frame, read by OpenImageIO and ffmpeg.

capabilities.capability: Inspect, edit and copy file metadata (timecode, camera and lens data, colour info) and pass it downstream.
capabilities.pro_use: Driving a comp from camera metadata, stamping timecode, tracking where an element came from.

match.note: Doodleberry records what shaped a film (provenance.json, licence classes, credits) and signs every final with C2PA content credentials holding it and the film's recipe (film.sign, film.verify, WP-26); per-frame image metadata such as timecode and lens data is not edited (WP-37).

capabilities.capability: Timecode and frame-number offsets on writes to match editorial.
capabilities.pro_use: Renders slot straight into the editor's timeline.

match.note: Hand-off timelines and EDLs carry the film's frame rate and timecode from zero; offsets to match an editorial start are WP-22.

capabilities.capability: Burned-in slates and shot information (text driven by metadata) for dailies.
capabilities.pro_use: Every review clip shows shot, version, frame and artist.

match.note: Storyboard contact sheets and critic packets carry shot notes and times beside stills; a burn-in on review video belongs with the review room (WP-19).

capabilities.capability: Resize an element to another format (fit width, fit height, fill or distort) with a choice of resampling filter.
capabilities.pro_use: Conforming plates and elements to the project's delivery format.

match.note: film.render with an aspect (16:9, 9:16, 1:1) re-stages characters and camera from the data instead of scaling or cropping; arbitrary sizes come from shots.json size.

capabilities.capability: Crop and bounding-box control, including letterboxing.
capabilities.pro_use: Limiting processing to the useful region and adding matte bars.

match.note: Bounding boxes are a raster-engine optimisation; Doodleberry never letterboxes by design (native dual-aspect composition).

capabilities.capability: Pixel aspect ratio handling for anamorphic and non-square formats.
capabilities.pro_use: Working on squeezed anamorphic plates.

match.note: Square-pixel social and web formats only.

capabilities.capability: Named format presets and custom formats.
capabilities.pro_use: Studio-wide delivery formats chosen from a list.

match.note: Aspect blocks and per-platform encoding profiles are data.

capabilities.capability: Viewer guides for title-safe and action-safe areas.
capabilities.pro_use: Keeping text and key action away from screen edges and platform overlays.

match.note: Layout QA measures text inside the safe area and heads cut by the frame; brand.assets also writes safe-area overlays for covers.

capabilities.capability: Arbitrary named channels grouped into layers beyond RGBA (up to 1023 per script), flowing through the tree together.
capabilities.pro_use: Carrying render passes, mattes, depth and motion vectors alongside the beauty image.

match.note: Masters carry named layers (beauty, line, fill, matte); depth, motion vectors and arbitrary channels are WP-37.

capabilities.capability: Shuffling channels between layers (Shuffle).
capabilities.pro_use: Pulling one render pass into RGB to grade or inspect it.

match.note: Needs a channel-aware compositor (WP-36).

capabilities.capability: Alpha handling with premultiply and unpremultiply to keep edges clean under colour correction.
capabilities.pro_use: Avoiding dark or bright fringes when grading a foreground element.

match.note: Internally Synfig and Grease Pencil characters are rendered with alpha and composited over the set video; user-level premultiplication control comes with the compositor (WP-36).

capabilities.capability: Copying channels from one stream to another (Copy, ChannelMerge).
capabilities.pro_use: Taking a matte from one render and applying it to another.

match.note: Falls within the named work package's scope.

capabilities.capability: Limiting any node to chosen channels and feeding a mask channel to it.
capabilities.pro_use: Grading only the alpha-masked region or only one pass.

match.note: Falls within the named work package's scope.

capabilities.capability: Utility passes such as depth (Z) and motion vectors as channels.
capabilities.pro_use: Driving depth of field, fog and motion blur in comp.

match.note: The bake already knows every layer's position and depth plane, so exact passes are possible; output of passes is WP-37, their use in DoF WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Layering one image over another with premultiplied alpha (the 'over' operation), with any number of inputs.
capabilities.pro_use: The basic operation of every comp: foreground over background.

match.note: Layer order is data the SVG player draws; shot.render composites Synfig/Grease Pencil characters over the set video.

capabilities.capability: A full set of blend operations (screen, multiply, plus, difference, minimum, maximum, overlay, hard light and more).
capabilities.pro_use: Adding light effects, combining passes, checking differences between versions.

match.note: Blend modes are in WP-36's scope; today only ffmpeg overlays are used.

capabilities.capability: Masked merges and a mix control for partial strength.
capabilities.pro_use: Applying an element only inside a matte or at reduced intensity.

match.note: Falls within the named work package's scope.

capabilities.capability: Matte-driven blend between two images (Keymix).
capabilities.pro_use: Swapping in a fixed region from another version or plate.

match.note: Falls within the named work package's scope.

capabilities.capability: Stencil and holdout operations that cut one element with another's alpha.
capabilities.pro_use: Hiding a foreground behind a set piece or cutting a shape out of a layer.

match.note: In pure 2D the z-order of parts and layers handles most occlusion; matte cut-outs need WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Bounding-box and metadata pass-through choices on merges.
capabilities.pro_use: Keeping processing regions small on large comps.

match.note: A raster performance concern; vector frames are drawn whole.

capabilities.capability: Contact sheets: tiling many images or frames into one image.
capabilities.pro_use: Reviewing many shots or versions at a glance.

match.note: qa.run writes contact sheets; film.storyboard writes strip.png and contact.pdf; critic.pack includes contact sheets.

capabilities.capability: Dissolving between two inputs over time.
capabilities.pro_use: Soft transitions and fades between shots or states.

match.note: Shot changes use whoosh cuts, and cross-dissolves, wipes, slides, dips and iris transitions (WP-15); match cuts are WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Analysing a plate's noise profile and removing noise while keeping detail.
capabilities.pro_use: Cleaning plates before keying and comp.

match.note: Frames drawn from vector data are noise-free; there are no camera plates.

capabilities.capability: Temporal denoising that uses neighbouring frames.
capabilities.pro_use: Removing noise from low-light footage.

match.note: No camera plates.

capabilities.capability: Denoise-then-regrain: re-adding a consistent grain so all elements share one texture.
capabilities.pro_use: Every element in the final comp looks like it came from the same camera.

match.note: Film-wide grain with a fixed seed (post finishing); it is uniform rather than matched to a plate.

capabilities.capability: Pulling a matte from blue or green screen footage with several keying algorithms.
capabilities.pro_use: Separating actors from screens for live-action composites.

match.note: No screen footage; characters are generated with exact alpha. (Act it out takes are read for pose only, never composited.)

capabilities.capability: Spill suppression and edge colour replacement.
capabilities.pro_use: Removing green contamination from hair and edges.

match.note: No screen footage.

capabilities.capability: Matte refinement: clipping black and white, separate core and edge mattes, combining with garbage mattes.
capabilities.pro_use: Getting a solid core and soft hair detail on the same key.

match.note: No screen footage.

capabilities.capability: Luminance or difference keying of high-contrast material, such as ink on paper.
capabilities.pro_use: Lifting drawn or printed elements off their background.

match.note: Scans and photos of drawings are flattened (divided by a blurred copy), ink is thresholded to alpha and specks removed.

capabilities.capability: GPU-accelerated keying that stays interactive on high-resolution plates.
capabilities.pro_use: Fast iteration on 4K screen shots.

match.note: No screen footage.

capabilities.capability: Animated Bezier and B-spline shapes as mattes, with per-point and global feather.
capabilities.pro_use: Isolating an element for grading, garbage mattes, articulated roto.

match.note: Masks are in WP-36's scope; in Doodleberry most mattes could be derived from part shapes rather than drawn.

capabilities.capability: Motion blur on roto shapes.
capabilities.pro_use: Mattes that match the blur of fast-moving elements.

match.note: Sub-frame motion blur in general is WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Clone and reveal painting for clean-up (rig removal, dust busting).
capabilities.pro_use: Removing rigs, wires and dust from plates.

match.note: No photographed plates to clean.

capabilities.capability: Paint strokes with brushes, erasers, blur and dodge/burn, with per-stroke lifetimes over frames.
capabilities.pro_use: Frame-by-frame touch-ups and painted effects.

match.note: Drawn levels, rough-line cleanup and painted effects are WP-35 (brush engines evaluated in WP-34).

capabilities.capability: Layer hierarchy of shapes and strokes with per-layer transforms and blend modes.
capabilities.pro_use: Organising hundreds of shapes for a character.

match.note: Falls within the named work package's scope.

capabilities.capability: Shapes linked to tracking data so mattes follow motion automatically.
capabilities.pro_use: A matte that rides on a tracked object with only small corrections.

match.note: Doodleberry knows every part's transform exactly, so WP-36 masks should attach to parts instead of tracks.

capabilities.capability: Cutting a still into separate layers with roto shapes.
capabilities.pro_use: Preparing a painting or photo for 2.5D moves.

match.note: Polygon cuts with overlap seams turn one drawing into separately animated parts.

capabilities.capability: 2D feature tracking of position, rotation and scale.
capabilities.pro_use: Measuring how something moves in footage.

match.note: No footage to track; the nearest thing is actout.clip reading body landmarks from reference takes for retargeting.

capabilities.capability: Match-moving: applying a track so an added element sticks to a moving feature.
capabilities.pro_use: Attaching signs, screens or effects to moving objects in a plate.

match.note: Everything's motion is known from the bake, so props attach to parts and bubble tails follow the speaker without tracking.

capabilities.capability: Stabilising shaky footage by inverting a track.
capabilities.pro_use: Steadying a plate before work, then re-applying the shake.

match.note: Only relevant to Act it out takes: WP-12 scopes camera-motion compensation from the background.

capabilities.capability: Four-point corner pinning of an image onto a moving surface.
capabilities.pro_use: Screen replacements and sign inserts.

match.note: Inserting an image onto a moving card in a scene needs WP-36 (or the 2.5D planes in WP-36).

capabilities.capability: Planar tracking of flat surfaces.
capabilities.pro_use: Robust tracks of walls, screens and floors.

match.note: No footage.

capabilities.capability: 3D camera solving from footage, with a point cloud.
capabilities.pro_use: Matching a CG camera to a real moving camera.

match.note: The virtual camera's keys are exact; nothing to solve.

capabilities.capability: Adding handheld motion or shake to a locked-off shot.
capabilities.pro_use: Making CG or locked shots feel filmed.

match.note: Seeded handheld drift and shake come from the camera grammar, deterministic per frame.

capabilities.capability: 2D transforms (translate, rotate, scale, skew) of any element, animatable, around a chosen centre.
capabilities.pro_use: Positioning and animating elements in the frame.

match.note: Character placement keys and kit element positions are data; parts transform through the rig.

capabilities.capability: Reframing the whole picture: pans, zooms and push-ins.
capabilities.pro_use: Camera moves on a static or animated frame.

match.note: Camera keys [t, [cx, cy, zoom]] are folded into the bake for every renderer; camera_auto adds follow, auto-framing and punch-ins.

capabilities.capability: Motion blur on transforms (shutter and sample controls).
capabilities.pro_use: Fast moves that read naturally.

match.note: Sub-frame motion blur on fast shots is WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Concatenating successive transforms so the image is filtered only once.
capabilities.pro_use: Avoiding softening from stacked transforms.

match.note: Vector parts are redrawn, never resampled; camera and placement are already folded into one baked transform.

capabilities.capability: Placing a flat element on a card in 3D space for perspective moves (Card3D).
capabilities.pro_use: Perspective tilts and 2.5D moves on stills.

match.note: scene.js films with a three.js scene exist (e.g. films/screwworm-3d); 2D layers on planes with a real camera are WP-36.

chapters.chapter: Warping images (GridWarp, SplineWarp, IDistort, LensDistortion, Smart Vectors)

capabilities.capability: Grid and spline warps to bend and reshape parts of an image.
capabilities.pro_use: Subtle shape fixes, cheating a pose, squash and stretch on elements.

match.note: Mesh parts deform with bones; per-part squash and stretch and angle-driven drawing substitution exist (v0.9). Grid and spline warps of images are WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Morphing between two images with matched shapes.
capabilities.pro_use: Transformations from one form into another.

match.note: WP-43 includes morphs between views (front to three-quarter to side).

capabilities.capability: Distortion driven by vectors, noise or UV maps (IDistort and displacement).
capabilities.pro_use: Heat haze, wobble and texture effects.

match.note: Line boil uses cycled smooth displacement fields with per-layer seeds, deterministic per frame.

capabilities.capability: Removing or adding lens distortion from grids or lines (LensDistortion).
capabilities.pro_use: Undistorting plates for tracking and redistorting CG to match.

match.note: No real lenses; a stylistic lens distortion, if wanted, would join WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Propagating paint or textures across a deforming surface with Smart Vectors.
capabilities.pro_use: Fixing faces or clothing across many frames from one painted frame.

match.note: No photographed surfaces; drawn parts already carry their own art.

chapters.chapter: Temporal operations, retiming and motion blur (Retime, FrameHold, Kronos, VectorGenerator, MotionBlur)

capabilities.capability: Retiming: speeding up, slowing down or reversing clips, with frame blending or optical-flow interpolation.
capabilities.pro_use: Slow-motion, speed changes to fit an edit.

match.note: Frames are pure functions of time, so retimes render exact in-between frames rather than interpolating; the warp works on SVG-player shots only.

capabilities.capability: Speed ramps: variable speed within a clip from a curve.
capabilities.pro_use: Ramping into slow motion on an impact.

match.note: Piecewise knots [[cut time, film time], ...]; film.soundoff writes them to hold lines long enough to read.

capabilities.capability: Freeze frames and holds.
capabilities.pro_use: Holding on a moment for emphasis or to fill time.

match.note: Holds play the acting slower rather than freezing; the QA bar fails any still stretch over 0.5 s, and camera holds are exact.

capabilities.capability: Slipping and offsetting clips in time.
capabilities.pro_use: Nudging an element's timing against the cut.

match.note: Times reference lines ('line.start+0.9'), so re-voicing slides everything together; timeline.edit moves clip layers.

capabilities.capability: Cutting and splicing clips (frame ranges, appending).
capabilities.pro_use: Building sequences and trims inside the comp tool.

match.note: film.render joins shots; film.cuts assembles cuts from edit.json with cut points on beats and never inside a line.

capabilities.capability: Generating motion vectors from footage for later use (VectorGenerator).
capabilities.pro_use: Feeding motion blur, retimes and Smart Vector tools.

match.note: Exact motion would come from the bake rather than estimation; its consumer, sub-frame motion blur, is WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Vector-based motion blur added in post (MotionBlur, Kronos).
capabilities.pro_use: Adding realistic blur to CG or fast moves without re-rendering.

match.note: Sub-frame motion blur on fast shots only is WP-15; cartoon speed lines and prop smear frames exist.

capabilities.capability: Frame blending and echoes for trails.
capabilities.pro_use: Ghosted trails and stylised motion.

match.note: Speed lines trail fast parts, props smear with ghosted multiples and draw motion arcs; frame blending is WP-15.

capabilities.capability: Frame-rate conversion and stepped timing.
capabilities.pro_use: Converting 24 fps material to 30 fps, or animating on twos.

match.note: Frames render natively at any fps; style.step 12 animates on twos (stepped frames are deduplicated). Rendering only unique stepped frames is WP-15.

chapters.chapter: Working with colour and OCIO colour management (incl. MatchGrade)

capabilities.capability: Primary grading: lift, gamma, gain, offset, and black and white points.
capabilities.pro_use: Balancing shots and setting the look.

match.note: shots.json post.grade takes ffmpeg filters (plus presets crisp, film, warm, cool, paper, noir), applied film-wide to the joined picture; per-shot and per-layer corrections are WP-36.

capabilities.capability: Range-based correction of shadows, midtones and highlights, with saturation and contrast.
capabilities.pro_use: Targeted fixes without keying.

match.note: Possible through ffmpeg filters in post.grade, film-wide only.

capabilities.capability: Curve-based correction: hue against saturation or luminance, and RGB curves.
capabilities.pro_use: Shifting one colour range, such as skies or skin.

match.note: ffmpeg curves and hue filters in post.grade; no per-layer curves.

capabilities.capability: Applying LUT files (.cube, .3dl).
capabilities.pro_use: Show looks and conversions supplied by the colourist.

match.note: A .cube LUT in post finishing.

capabilities.capability: OCIO colour management: a working space, input transforms per file, output transforms, any config.
capabilities.pro_use: Consistent colour across every department and tool.

match.note: OpenColorIO working space ACEScg with the sRGB texture input transform and display transforms back (film.master, film.from_master).

capabilities.capability: ACES workflows (ACEScg working space; ACES 2.0 in Nuke 17).
capabilities.pro_use: Industry-standard colour pipeline for VFX and features.

match.note: ACEScg masters under the ACES 2.1 studio config (OpenColorIO 2.6).

capabilities.capability: Viewer display transforms and looks.
capabilities.pro_use: Viewing the same linear data as it will appear on each display.

match.note: The ACES 2.1 output transform is offered as a review view (view=aces); looks are WP-37.

capabilities.capability: CDL import and export for grading round trips.
capabilities.pro_use: Matching the on-set or editorial grade in comp.

match.note: Falls within the named work package's scope.

capabilities.capability: Scopes: histogram, waveform and vectorscope.
capabilities.pro_use: Measuring levels and colour objectively instead of by eye.

match.note: image.scopes draws an RGB histogram, a luma waveform and a vectorscope for a frame, with clipping figures.

capabilities.capability: Automatic colour matching of one shot to a reference (MatchGrade, NukeX).
capabilities.pro_use: Matching inserts and pick-ups to the hero shot.

match.note: Colour is palette data so shots already agree; a colour script and grades per scene are WP-37, palette variants WP-16.

capabilities.capability: Blurs: Gaussian, directional, per-channel sizes.
capabilities.pro_use: Softening elements, faking depth, building glows.

match.note: Blurs are in WP-36's scope.

capabilities.capability: Depth-driven defocus with realistic bokeh (ZDefocus, Defocus).
capabilities.pro_use: Depth of field matched to a lens, pulling focus between planes.

match.note: WP-36 adds multiplane depth of field.

capabilities.capability: Convolution with a custom kernel image for lens-shaped blur (Convolve).
capabilities.pro_use: Bokeh in the shape of a real aperture.
